title: 3.5.24 Lab: Parallel-Arrays-vs-Object Refactor
description: Refactor three parallel arrays into one array of records, then read the fields back with a dot. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Start from the parallel arrays
steps.instructions: The starter keeps three separate arrays, one per field, aligned by index: a name, a score and a group for each player. Read it and see how each field is fetched from a different array at the same index.

steps.title: Collapse them into one array of records
steps.instructions: Replace the three parallel arrays with a single array called players whose elements are objects, each object holding name, score and group for one player.

steps.title: Read each record with a dot
steps.instructions: Loop over the new array and print each player's fields with bracket index then dot field, so all three fields come from one record.

requirements.title: array of object records built
requirements.description: An array literal holds object literals. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Build one array whose elements are objects. Each object holds the name, score and group for one player.

requirements.title: record fields read with a dot
requirements.description: Reads arr[i].field. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Pick a record with its index, then read each field with a dot: the array, [i], a dot, the field name.

requirements.title: loop over players prints each record
requirements.description: A loop over the players array prints each record. Help: 3.3.5 (Looping Over Arrays (for / for…of))
requirements.hint: Loop over players (for or for...of) and print inside the loop, so each record is printed by the loop.

requirements.title: output printed
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: players holds one record per player, with the same data
requirements.description: players is the three records { name, score, group } for Marisol, Dev and Priya, in that order, and the program prints each player. Help: 3.5.23 (Example: Record Shape)
requirements.hint: Build players as an array of three objects with the keys name, score and group, using the values from the old arrays in the same order. Delete the old parallel arrays.

requirements.title: the parallel arrays are gone
requirements.description: The old names, scores and groups arrays are deleted: players is the only place the data lives. Help: 3.5.2 (Grouping Related Values)
requirements.hint: Once players holds everything, delete the three old arrays. If they are still there, the program still has two copies of the data.
